name: HamidReza Saadi Dadmarzi

bio: I am HamidReza Saadi Dadmarzi, an M.Sc. student in Computer Science at Koç University and a researcher in cryptography. My work is centered on password-based authentication, secure multi-party computation, post-quantum protocols, and privacy-preserving machine learning. I like problems where theory, proofs, and systems all have to fit together: a protocol should be formally meaningful, implementable, and measurable.
summary: I design and analyze cryptographic protocols for authentication and privacy in distributed systems. My current research focuses on MPC-based password authentication, robust/updatable authentication, post-quantum SSO and IoT authenticated key exchange, and privacy-preserving learning. I also build Rust/Go prototypes and benchmark harnesses so that protocol claims can be tested against realistic implementation costs.

researchAreas.title: Multi-Party Computation(MPC) & Distributed Systems
researchAreas.question: How can password authentication remain secure when secrets are distributed, updateable, and exposed to malicious infrastructure?
researchAreas.summary: This line studies password-authentication protocols that split trust across servers while supporting updates, robustness, and performance measurement. My contribution is at the protocol-design/proof boundary, plus the systems side: Rust/Go implementations, Dockerized experiments, and reproducible benchmarks.

projects.title: UpSPA: Secure and Updatable Single Password Authentication
projects.summary: UpSPA is the core protocol line, and the full-stack prototype is its real-case application: a decentralized password-manager browser extension built around UpSPA. The current product target is the browser extension; mobile and desktop clients are planned future products once the extension workflow is stable.

projects.title: RoUpSPA: Robust Updatable Single Password Authentication
projects.summary: A robustness-oriented continuation of UpSPA, focused on making updatable password authentication resilient to failure and malicious behavior in distributed deployments.

publications: UpSPA: Secure and Updatable Single Password Authentication
RoUpSPA: Robust Updatable Single Password Authentication

researchAreas.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
researchAreas.question: What does authentication look like when password-protected systems and IoT protocols must survive the post-quantum transition?
researchAreas.summary: My PQC work is about taking post-quantum tools beyond primitives and into application-level protocol models: password-protected SSO, KEM-based authentication, and mechanizable security frameworks for constrained IoT protocols.

projects.title: QuasarSSO / KEMSSO: Post-Quantum Password-Protected SSO
projects.summary: A post-quantum password-protected single-sign-on direction that uses KEM-centered design to reason about authentication in the post-quantum setting, while keeping the password-authentication story connected to deployable SSO workflows.

projects.title: AEGIS: Mechanizable Framework for PQ IoT AKE
projects.summary: A framework for comparing security analyses of post-quantum IoT authenticated key-exchange protocols. It makes the threat model explicit: state leakage, desynchronization, downgrade attacks, energy exhaustion, KCI/UKS resistance, and standard AKE secrecy.

publications: QuasarSSO: A Post-Quantum Password-Protected SSO System
AEGIS: A Mechanizable Framework for Post-Quantum IoT Authenticated Key Exchange

researchAreas.title: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning(PPML)
researchAreas.question: How can learning systems expose less data while staying efficient enough for real distributed training pipelines?
researchAreas.summary: This line connects cryptographic privacy and machine learning systems. I present CURE and DPFL/SpectraDP as complementary directions: one based on FHE tooling and one based on communication-efficient differential privacy for federated learning.

projects.title: CURE: Privacy-Preserving ML with FHE
projects.summary: Work on privacy-preserving ML using Lattigo in Go, including implementation/debugging of CKKS-based FHE and bootstrapping modules. This section highlights my ability to move between crypto libraries, engineering details, and ML privacy goals.

projects.title: DPFL / SpectraDP: Spectral Trade-offs for Communication-Efficient Differentially Private Learning
projects.summary: A frequency-domain / spectral approach to differentially private federated learning, aimed at reducing communication while preserving principled DP accounting and model utility.

publications: SpectraDP: Spectral Trade-offs for Communication-Efficient Differentially Private Learning
